answer: Squaring earned reputation makes splitting one history across fake seats a losing trade. A seat's vote and payout weight is R^2, where R counts its own passed graded tasks, capped at one per epoch and never transferable, for example a cedar timber estimate, a meadow flood-risk map or a mesa erosion survey. An operator dividing R among n clones keeps n(R/n)^2 = R^2/n: 10 clones hold 10% of one honest seat's weight, 100 hold 1%. Restoring full weight means each clone separately passes its own graded task every epoch, a per-seat cost that cannot be pooled or waited out.
